summary: Route P (settled-context scheduling) planned across 15 phases, 42 hours. The plan does not edit blockingWorldS4Keyed's comparison predicate at all; it changes when a minting shape may fire. Research risk (c) is discharged by replacing the report's recursive per-world settledness predicate with a global, non-recursive one: a mint fires only when no non-minting rule can fire anywhere on the branch. That is decidable by direct computation, strictly stronger than the per-world condition, and carries no well-foundedness obligation -- which matters because the accessibility record cannot supply one (mint edges point to strictly larger fresh worlds but redirect edges may point to smaller ones, and reflexive self-blocks are permitted, so the predecessor relation can cycle). The ordered stepper is built as a parallel definition so the landed completeness line stays green at every checkpoint; the superseded driver is retired only in the final phase, with a proved replacement for every deletion.
decisions_made: Phase 1 lands the counterexample as a permanent CslibTests/S4LoopGuardRegression.lean corpus BEFORE any code change, using the #guard_msgs in #eval idiom already established by CslibTests/TableauConformance.lean. #eval works from CslibTests/ but not from inside the Tableau directory, so the test surface, not a chained-rfl proof term, is the right home. Phase 1 asserts the CURRENT (unsound) CLOSED verdict marked KNOWN-UNSOUND so the checkpoint stays green; Phase 8 flips it.

Risk (c) resolved by a global mint-readiness predicate rather than the report's per-world recursive one. Enabled by modalApplyOneS4Rules (FrameRules.lean:158) returning .notApplicable when a persistent rule's output is empty, so settledness is expressible even though persistent formulas never enter the expanded set.

The ordered stepper's traversal is two-stage: findSome? over the non-mint candidate list first, falling back to the LITERAL old b.findSome? traversal. This yields modalStepBranchS4KeyedOrdered_eq_none_iff, which makes the completeness line's saturation step transfer definitionally instead of needing the modalHintikkaSetGen conjuncts re-derived from scratch. That lemma is the single largest cost reduction on risk (b).

Risk (a) is expected to be tractable: modalExpMeasure_step_lt_S4Keyed (LoopChecking.lean:6455) consumes only 'selected sf is in the branch', 'sf is not in the expanded set', and the result-shape case split -- it never uses which sf. The traversal shape matters in exactly one place, the projection bridge modalStepBranchS4Keyed_proj_stepBranchGen (:6345), which has exactly one consumer. Phase 5 replaces the bridge, not the measure argument.

Phase 8 is an explicit abort gate: the reordering must be shown empirically to open the counterexample, and the size-<=6 sweep must show zero open-to-closed verdict changes, BEFORE any soundness proof work is invested.

The soundness invariant weakening is additive: branchSatisfiableIn (FrameSoundness.lean:111) is left exactly as is and remains what K/T/B/5 consume; branchPropAdequateIn is a new, strictly weaker sibling used only by the S4 keyed line.
flagged_theorem_changes: Phase 14 ADDS modalTableauS4KeyedOrdered_complete beside the landed modalTableauS4Keyed_complete (FrameCompleteness.lean:4249); the landed theorem is not weakened.

Phase 15 is the only destructive phase: it deletes modalStepBranchS4Keyed, modalExpandBranchesS4Keyed, modalTableauS4Keyed, modalTableauS4Keyed_complete and their stepper-specific support lemmas -- each with a proved ordered replacement. Removal-with-replacement, never weakening. If any consumer lacks a counterpart, the declaration is retained and the gap reported.
Phase 6 states that if keysUpdate_preserves_keysDistinct or blockingWorldS4Keyed_none_fresh needs weakening, that contradicts the plan's central claim and must be escalated rather than worked around.
No phase may discharge an obligation with sorry, an axiom, or a vacuous statement; Phase 10 in particular names its hardest obligation and mandates [BLOCKED] escalation over a stub.
dead_ends: Route Q (split accessibility record) is not planned: the research rejects it as strictly worse, reducing to Route P's step-2 obligation with extra bookkeeping.
No phase edits blockingWorldS4Keyed's comparison predicate; every local guard edit was refuted in research.
